quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Lean when the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator. They should hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never touch the operator.
Sit as far back on their seat as possible.
Hold onto their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a passenger, tell them to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking alcohol, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities instead of drinking.
Keep them from leaving until they are sober.
Let them ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can prevent someone from riding while impaired by arranging another way for them to get home, keeping them busy with other activities, and stopping them from leaving until they are sober. You can also ask other friends to help.

questions.question: How should you maintain control of your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright.
Look ahead through the turn.
Stop completely before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn.
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, look ahead through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is typically a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show traffic rules, such as speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Brake slowly.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean forward. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: When riding at night, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Use your high beam, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce speed and increase your following distance to avoid collisions. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam headlight when not following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. To shift up to a higher gear, lift the shift lever with your foot. To shift down, press it down.

questions.question: Why should group riders avoid pairing up?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections can make it hard for riders to see.
Riders cannot maneuver safely in pairs.
Left-side riders cannot safely exit the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders cannot maneuver safely in pairs.
questions.explanation: Group riders should not ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough space to avoid hazards.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop until it loses interest.
Swerve around it.
Approach slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, shift to a lower gear and approach it slowly. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space cushion and makes you visible to others.
Gives you more space and makes you visible to others.
Increases your risk of hitting hazards and lets others pass you.
Reduces your risk of hitting hazards and lets you follow closely behind another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you more space and makes you visible to others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and let them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should stop other drivers from trying to share your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears. Choose a lane position that gives you the most space.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may finish the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen within speed limits and only where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To lower the chance of a crash, do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be visible.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Be ready to react to hazards.
Hope another driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure you are visible and other drivers know what you plan to do. Use proper signals and good lane position. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Watch ahead and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay out of the left portion of the lane.
Always stay out of the right portion of the lane.
Always stay out of the center portion of the lane.
Use whichever part of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever part of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothes, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: As a beginning rider following another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay at least four seconds behind the other vehicle.
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible.
Not worry about how far back you are.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay at least four seconds behind the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should stay at least four seconds behind another vehicle. Stay even further back when road or weather conditions are bad.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Makes a rider look cool.
Is usually too hot to wear when riding.
Protects you in a crash.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally made of leather, when riding. Leather jackets can also help prevent dehydration in warm weather. Many motorcycle jackets are made to keep you cool even when it is hot.

questions.question: If a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: It means they see you.
It will never happen.
It does not mean they will let you pass safely.
It means they will let you pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will let you pass safely.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at a motorcycle but do not notice it.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the car ahead, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Weave back and forth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of your lane. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a clear view of the shoulder.
Make it hard to see road hazards.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you and you can see them. Never stay in another driver's blind spot for long.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?

options.text: After you start the motorcycle
Before you start the motorcycle
While you are riding
At a traffic signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
Apply your brakes slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when wobbling because it makes the problem worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane behind a car:

options.text: The driver is likely to see you.
The driver will only see you if they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You are stopping other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will only see you if they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This way, the driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirror, so this position helps you stay visible.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: It may be hard to reach a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you. They could change lanes into you without warning. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.
